archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose passing is accurate and careful from the pocket, and whose biggest single source of value is breaking the pocket and running when a play stalls, more than designed runs.

report.headline: Accuracy is back and the ball is safe; sacks and third downs cap him.
report.take:
Daniels in 2026 sits between the two versions of himself we have already seen. The 2024 rookie posted 0.204 EPA a play, ninth in the league, with 891 rushing yards. The 2025 version slid to 0.029 with a -2.7 CPOE. This year's passer is accurate again: a 4.51 CPOE ranks 9th of 49, a gain of 7.2 points on last season. He has thrown zero interceptions, and his bad-throw rate is down a point. His passing EPA per dropback, though, is a pedestrian 0.015, 24th. Accuracy with no turnovers should produce more than that, so the question is what is eating it.

Mostly it is sacks and third downs. He is taking sacks on 8.2% of dropbacks (33rd), and 8 of the 16 came on third down. There he has -15.5 EPA total and converts only 30.9% while facing an average of 7.9 yards to go. In one-score games his EPA is -0.088 a play with 13 sacks. Down two scores he is at 0.192 with a 15.2 CPOE, which is the softer coverage you get when trailing, not a clutch gene. Two other drags show up: screens and throws behind the line (-7.5 EPA on 20 throws) and a red zone that nets exactly zero EPA on 46.4% completions. The real value is in the middle of the field. On throws of 10-19 air yards he has a 14.1 CPOE and 0.53 EPA a throw, his best skill this season.

The legs paper over a lot. His dropbacks total 15.7 EPA against only 2.9 from passing alone, and the gap is the scrambles: 24 of them for 250 yards, 11 first downs, 0.793 EPA each. Designed runs have done nothing (5 plays, zero successes). He is a creator, not a zone-read back. The sack problem is also less a pocket flaw than it looks. His pressure-to-sack rate of 30% is far better than the 41-44% of his first two seasons, so he is escaping more than he used to. He is simply getting pressured on early downs and stuck in long third downs behind an offense that ranks 25th in success rate.

The last three games tilt the picture. He is throwing more and better (263.3 yards a game, 7.6 YPA, 6.3 CPOE), but the rushing has dried up to 16.3 yards a game, 25.7 under his season mark, and the sacks have ticked up to 3.3 a game. His season rushing line leans heavily on a 103-yard, two-touchdown day against the Giants, his next opponent.

strengths.title: Intermediate accuracy carrying the offense
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards have been his best play type by a distance: a 63.6% success rate, a 14.1 CPOE and 17.5 EPA total, more than his deep and short throws combined. That is the main reason his CPOE has rebounded from last year's slump. It fits his rookie profile and is a skill, not a small-sample fluke, though 33 attempts is still a modest base.

strengths.title: Scrambles as the escape valve
strengths.body: Twenty-four scrambles at 0.793 EPA apiece, with 11 first downs, are the gap between a below-average passer line and a useful dropback line. They also explain why his pressure-to-sack rate is far better than in past seasons. Extending plays has turned would-be sacks into chunk runs. This is a career-long trait, so it should hold whenever the coverage turns its back.

strengths.title: Ball security, so far spotless
strengths.body: There are no interceptions through six games and no interception-worthy throws charted, against a league interception rate of 2.4%. The care is real: his bad-throw rate is down and he lives on short and intermediate throws. The zero itself won't last, since he threw 9 as a rookie. Expect a low interception rate rather than none.

concerns.title: Third downs and sacks stall drives
concerns.body: Third down has cost him 15.5 EPA, with a 30.9% conversion rate and half his sacks. Those long distances are partly a product of an offense that struggles on early downs, and his pressure-to-sack rate is better than ever. Still, an 8.2% sack rate ranking 33rd caps his efficiency every week. This is part role, part flaw, and it is the main thing between him and his 2024 level.

concerns.title: Red-zone and touchdown production lagging
concerns.body: His 3.9% TD rate ranks 29th, and red-zone plays add up to exactly zero EPA on 46.4% completions. All seven touchdown passes came on short throws, and the deep ball is hitting only 30.8% of the time. On 28 red-zone plays this is likely to improve some, but not to rookie levels while the offense ranks in the low 20s.

concerns.title: Rushing has dried up lately
concerns.body: Over the last three games he is running for 16.3 yards a game, well under his season rate, and designed runs have been a dead end all year. Without the scramble yards, both his real value and his fantasy floor shrink, because his passing EPA alone is roughly league average. Whether this is game plan, coverage or caution, it is the swing variable for his outlook.

trend.note: His passing EPA has swung from +3.9 to -3.9 game to game, and his best two passing efforts came against a top-10 and a bottom-6 defense alike. Lately the passing volume and accuracy are up while the rushing and sacks are moving the wrong way, capped by a -3.9 EPA, four-sack, lost-fumble day against the Rams.

nextGame.headline: Short-week Giants rematch: deep shots closed, scramble lanes open
nextGame.body:
The Giants are a down-to-down defense. They rank 5th in success rate allowed and 3rd against deep passes, and they give up just 218.8 passing yards a game to quarterbacks, 3rd fewest. That takes away his weakest area, the deep ball, and pushes him toward the intermediate throws where he has been best. They also rarely hit the quarterback (28th in hit rate), they allow explosive runs at the 26th-ranked rate, and quarterbacks score plenty of fantasy points against them through touchdowns. In the first meeting the Giants blitzed him 22 times and sacked him five times, and he answered with 103 rushing yards and two scores. Expect a modest passing line with his ceiling tied to the legs. Their offense is heavily run-leaning, which shortens games, and the total is a low 42.5. A drizzle-chance forecast with light winds is a minor nuisance, not a game-changer.

Availability matters on both sides. Washington is thin at receiver: Treylon Burks is out and Dyami Brown is on IR, which concentrates targets on Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, his two most efficient options. Tight end Chig Okonkwo (hip, limited) is questionable against a defense that holds tight ends 3 points under their norm. Guard Lucas Patrick is questionable after a concussion, a real risk to protection on four days' rest. For the Giants, linebacker Abdul Carter, an 87%-snap starter, is questionable; his absence would lighten the front Daniels has to escape.

keyMatchups.title: Intermediate game vs stingy deep coverage
keyMatchups.body: The Giants rank 3rd against deep passes and 7th in explosive pass rate, so long shots are unlikely to pay. His 10-19 yard throws are where he can win, and Diggs and Williams are the receivers producing on them. If he gets impatient and forces it deep, the efficiency drops off.

keyMatchups.title: Blitz rematch and the scramble lanes
keyMatchups.body: Week 5 brought heavy blitzing, five sacks and a 29.7% pressure rate, but also his best rushing day of the season. This defense allows explosive runs at a high rate, and his scrambles are worth 0.793 EPA each. Whether the legs reappear after three quiet weeks decides whether this is a 15-point or a 25-point game.

keyMatchups.title: Low-total, run-heavy game script
keyMatchups.body: The Giants' offense runs far more than situation predicts, and the total is 42.5, which points to fewer possessions and fewer dropbacks. Washington is a short underdog, so a close game keeps him in the one-score state where his EPA has been negative. Volume passing is unlikely unless he falls behind.

nextGame.watch: Whether he scrambles again: early-down designed scrambles and third-and-long escapes against a blitzing front are his path to a big game.

restOfSeason.body:
The accuracy rebound looks real. It matches his rookie profile, it shows up across depths, and his bad-throw rate is down, so a CPOE in the mid-single digits should hold. The zero interceptions will not: expect a low but nonzero rate. The touchdown rate should lift a little from 29th as red-zone luck evens out. The sack rate is the stubborn part. He is escaping pressure better than ever, but the offense keeps leaving him in long third downs, and Patrick's status plus a thin receiver room don't help.

The biggest variable is the rushing. The season rate is propped up by one 103-yard game, and the last three weeks are far below it. A realistic projection splits the difference: around 200-250 passing yards with roughly one to one-and-a-half touchdowns a game, and rushing that fluctuates from game to game but averages somewhere in the 20s to 40s. That makes him a solid weekly fantasy starter whose ceiling depends on his legs, not a return to his 2024 efficiency unless the third-down sacks come down.
swingFactors: Sack rate on third downs and O-line health
Receiver depth with Burks and Brown out

confidence.note: Six games, missed time early, and a rushing line skewed by one big day.
